pr.title: Treat an empty owner as no owner
pr.head: d55275dcdf4a77734fe90d84cdf8e7f414445666

summary: Every Projector project has a plan file, docs/projects/<name>/readme.md, whose YAML frontmatter holds its status, its priority, and an optional owner, the one person who owns the project. The project command reads that frontmatter for list, show, and check, and rewrites single lines of it for status, priority, owner, and done.

Before this change, a plan with an owner: line and no value was invalid. project check rejected it with "owner must not be empty", and every command that loads the plan before writing refused too. That included project owner <name> --clear, the command meant to remove the line, so the only fix was a hand edit.

This change reads an empty owner as no owner. owner:, owner: with trailing spaces, owner: "", and a quoted blank such as owner: ' ' all load with owner: null. check accepts them, and list --owner never selects them. project owner fills in the value on the existing line, and --clear removes the line. A multi-line owner, such as owner: |, is still an error.

The change also fixes a bug with CRLF line endings, where each line ends in a carriage return and a newline. The pattern that finds a field's line missed it on such a plan unless the line ended in a comment. project owner then added a second owner: line, which made the plan unreadable, and status and priority refused to update it.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One Projector review, of d55275d, found the head clean, with no finding threads.
  • The full unit suite (927 tests, 1 skipped), project check, both claude plugin validate runs, and git diff --check passed on this head.
  • #310, which documents hand-repairing a plan the commands cannot load, uses status: blocked as its example and touches none of these files, so the two can merge in either order.

groups.title: Reading and writing the owner line
groups.kicker: The loader accepts an empty owner, and the writer fills it in on the same line
intro: All of the change's behavior lives in src/projector/core.py. Three pieces change:

1. The loader. project_from_text turns a plan's text into a Project. It no longer rejects an empty owner, and it stores an owner that is blank after stripping as None.
  2. The writer. ProjectStore.set_owner backs project owner. When the existing value is empty, it rebuilds the line as owner: <login>, with one space after the colon and a space before any trailing comment.
  3. The field-line pattern. _field_line builds the regular expression that status, priority, and owner use to find their line. It now allows a carriage return before the line end.

files.note: The loader, the owner writer, and the shared field-line pattern.

checks.text: The lookahead (?=\r?$) leaves the carriage return outside the match. I traced the three writers that use the pattern: the value replacement in _set_field, the --clear removal, which cuts through the newline, and the priority insertion in _insert_priority. Each keeps CRLF endings intact, and a scratch run of owner on CRLF plans wrote owner: ben\r\n every time.

Every reader of Project.owner already handles None: list --owner, search, the text listing, and the site's owner label. An absent owner defaults to "" at line 265, which still passes the multi-line test.

In a scratch repository I ran project owner alpha ben on owner:# c, owner: followed by a tab, owner: '' # c, owner: " ", and owner:, with LF and with CRLF endings. Each left one owner: ben line, with any comment kept after a space, and project check passed afterward.
Only an empty value is rebuilt. A non-empty value, such as "" or ' ', is replaced in place, and the existing prefix already holds the space after the colon.

groups.title: Tests for each empty form and for CRLF plans
groups.kicker: New tests pin the exact file contents each command writes
intro: The tests create plans in temporary Git repositories and run the CLI against them. They compare the whole file after each command, so a stray space, a doubled line, or a lost carriage return fails the test.

files.note: Five new mutation tests, one renamed validation test, and the loader test's empty-owner plan moved to the valid side.

checks.text: This test covers the CRLF fix. It runs owner and then status on a CRLF plan and compares the bytes.
The loader test checks that project_from_text and the store load a plan the same way. The empty-owner plan now loads, so the expected failure count drops by one.

groups.title: Command reference
groups.kicker: The CLI reference describes how an empty owner reads
intro: docs/cli.md is the reference for every project command. It gains a paragraph on the empty owner and drops "an empty" from the list of owner problems check reports.

files.note: A new paragraph on how an empty owner reads, and one fewer check error.

checks.text: Each claim in this paragraph matches the code at this head and the scratch runs above. No other document, skill, or template still calls an empty owner an error.
